results.title: New tariffs test Georgia’s global trade resilience
results.content:
The White House initially established 10% tariffs on imports from all countries, along with higher “reciprocal” tariffs targeting nations such as China, Vietnam and members of the European Union that levy tariffs on U.S. goods. Mexico and Canada — Georgia’s top export destinations — were spared from the new tariffs. [...] In 2024, the Peach State ranked seventh nationwide in net exports, shipping around $53.1 billion in locally made products overseas while importing about $145.6 billion, according to the Georgia Chamber of Commerce.

President Donald Trump’s newly unveiled tariffs have sent shockwaves through the manufacturing, technology and agricultural sectors across the country — particularly in Georgia. [...] Chinese tariffs could especially affect local businesses, the Georgia chamber noted. China was the third largest buyer of local goods last year at $3 billion, behind Canada and Mexico, and the second highest importer to Georgia at $17.2 billion.

On April 3, the chamber published a report outlining the impacts local industries may experience from the tariffs, including higher prices for car parts and steel, a squeeze on crop imports and possible slowdowns at the state’s bustling ports.
